statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is exactly the sorted list of occupied final positions. Define final(x) for an initial position x by starting with y = x and, for i = 0, 1, ..., len(moveFrom)-1 in that order, setting y := moveTo[i] if y = moveFrom[i] and leaving y unchanged otherwise; set final(x) to the final y. Then (a) for every k with 0 <= k < len(r), there exists j with 0 <= j < len(nums) and r[k] = final(nums[j]); (b) for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums), there exists k with 0 <= k < len(r) and r[k] = final(nums[j]); and (c) for every k with 0 <= k+1 < len(r), r[k] < r[k+1].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; len(moveFrom) >= 1; len(moveFrom) = len(moveTo); len(nums) <= 100000; len(moveFrom) <= 100000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums), 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(moveFrom), 1 <= moveFrom[i] <= 1000000000 and 1 <= moveTo[i] <= 1000000000; and the problem's promise holds: just before each step i with 0 <= i < len(moveFrom), at least one marble is at moveFrom[i].
